issue.title: [Bug] git_log ignores branch argument and mislabels current-branch commits

steps: Initialize a local Git repository. Configure user.name Fixture and user.email fixture@example.com. Commit base.txt with message BASE, create branch other, add other.txt and commit OTHER_ONLY there, then return to the original branch and commit current.txt with message CURRENT_ONLY.
Call git_log with branch="other" and count=5. Report the raw result.
expected: The requested branch history includes OTHER_ONLY and excludes CURRENT_ONLY.
defect: git_log labels the result as branch other but actually displays current-branch commits.

fault location.explanation: executeGitLog uses args.branch for the heading but does not pass that value into getCommits, so git log still runs against HEAD. 835a3a41 propagates the branch argument.

Root cause: executeGitLog uses args.branch for the heading but does not pass that value into getCommits, so git log still runs against HEAD. 835a3a41 propagates the branch argument.

_meta.notes: Self-contained two-branch fixture follows the issue operation. Keep the checked-out branch distinct from other at the time of git_log.
